findings.point: а (criteria compatible only through an unnamed mechanism, AP-016), г/design completeness
findings.where: REQ-108 criterion 8 (the server started on a database whose role has rolsuper or rolbypassrls true exits ≠ 0), criterion 12 (compose has exactly db `postgres:17` and web; the start command runs migrate, then node-main with NODE_ENV=production; GET / → 200 and the row 0001_init.sql), criterion 7/8 (0001 creates only the NOLOGIN group roles sai_app and sai_preview); REQ-109 criterion 6 (the smoke in the docker job needs /api/health 200, so role "ok").
findings.problem: The block never says which database login role the server uses outside PGlite. The official postgres image creates POSTGRES_USER «with superuser power» (docker-library docs, read 2026-11-17, not measured), so with the selfcheck of criterion 8 the web service of criterion 12 exits at start (or, if the selfcheck were lazy, /api/health answers role "unsafe" 503 and the smoke of REQ-109 criterion 6 fails). ARCH §4 names the way out (a login role sai_app_login, LOGIN NOSUPERUSER NOBYPASSRLS, made by 0001 with APP_DB_PASSWORD; migrations as the owner role through DATABASE_URL_UNPOOLED, ARCH §19.6), but the block neither requires it nor lists it under «Not covered»; the files list allows no init script («services db and web only»), and no criterion says which URL migrate uses and which node-main uses in the container. The same question decides the first production deploy (spike S3 reads the Neon role later). Besides, ARCH §18 puts the «role selfcheck» into the real-Postgres level, while criterion 8 tests the selfcheck only in app/test/int with injected readings; app/test/pg has no case with a real superuser login. The designer must guess between a login role made by 0001, a compose init file, or a selfcheck that reads another role — the last would weaken the ground of Q8.
findings.needed: The block names the runtime login role for compose and CI (and the variables and files it needs: for example the ARCH §4 role with APP_DB_PASSWORD and the two URLs for migrate and node-main), with a criterion that pins it (docker job: web connects as a role with rolsuper and rolbypassrls false, migrate as the owner); criterion 8 gains a real-Postgres case in app/test/pg (a superuser login → refused, the dedicated login → passes); or the block states plainly that this is out of scope and how criteria 12 and REQ-109/6 are then met.

findings.point: д (Q10: a realistic failure), б (ARCH §14.9 item 4, decisions/0092 item 7)
findings.where: REQ-109 criterion 8: «with MIGRATE_ON_BUILD=1 the steps run in the order migrate, then check-public … a failing migrate → exit ≠ 0 and check-public is not run … with SITE_GATE=closed the output folder is left serving only the gate page».
findings.problem: The criterion does not say what the build does when SITE_GATE=closed and the database is unreachable. As written, with MIGRATE_ON_BUILD=1 (the production value of ARCH §19.3) migrate always runs first and a failed migrate fails the build. The owner's emergency close (incident.md: set SITE_GATE, then `vercel redeploy`, which rebuilds — decisions/0092 item 7) then fails exactly when the database is down, and the open deployment stays live. ARCH §14.9 item 4 says SITE_GATE=closed «closes the whole site even when the database is unreachable». The letter of criterion 8 forbids the obvious fix (no migrate while closed).
findings.needed: Criterion 8 states the order with SITE_GATE closed (for example: no migrate while closed, or a failed migrate does not stop the gate output) and adds the test row «SITE_GATE=closed and a failing migrate → exit 0, the output is the gate page».

findings.point: а (the check does not give its stated result; Q6)
findings.where: REQ-108 criterion 2: «# fail 0» and «# skipped 0» in both test steps and `grep -rnE '\.(skip|todo|only)\(|(skip|todo|only): *true' app/test` → no line; REQ-109 criterion 10: the same two lines and only `grep -rnE '\.(skip|todo|only)\(' app/test`.

The skip string is caught by «# skipped 0», but a node:test case with `{ todo: "later" }` and a failing body gives «# fail 0», «# skipped 0», «# todo 1» and exit 0 (measured with node v22.23.4). So a disabled test passes all three checks. REQ-109 criterion 10's grep misses the option forms `skip: true`, `only: true`, `todo: true` too.
findings.needed: Both criteria also require «# todo 0», and the grep covers the option forms with any value other than false (or names that an option with a string value is forbidden); the two greps of the run are the same.

findings.point: а (a ban without a named comparison form, AP-120)
findings.where: REQ-108 criterion 3: «a `fetch(` in any file of app/server or app/api» is red; «a file of app/server importing anything but app/public/shared/**, node:* …, hono, @hono/node-server, pg, zod, fflate»; app/public/shared «naming `document` or `window`».
findings.problem: The ban names neither the comparison form nor what counts. On a planted app/api/index.js in the two natural entry shapes (`export default { fetch(request) {…} }` and a wrapper that restores `__p` and calls `app.fetch(new Request(…))`), the literal text gives 2 hits, a whole-identifier match also 2, and a «not after a dot» rule still 1 (the method definition). REQ-109 criterion 2 makes the entry restore the path and call the app, and decisions/0116 О4 leaves the export shape to the design; the ban decides it silently. Also, literally, a file of app/server may import none of app/server's own files (createApp must import the route table), and it is not said whether a package means the bare name only or also its subpaths (`hono/…`, `@hono/node-server/…`; the block names `hono/vercel` as a separate name). `document`/`window` as words would also hit names such as `windowSize`. The analyst's own assessment says «the bans compare by identifier borders (AP-120)»; criterion 3 does not.
findings.needed: Criterion 3 names the form of each rule: the outside call is a call of the global fetch (an identifier not preceded by `.` and not a method or property name, and `globalThis.fetch`), with planted twins `app.fetch(` and `fetch(request) {` that stay green; own-folder imports of app/server are allowed explicitly; the package rule says bare name or name plus subpath; `document`/`window` as whole identifiers.

findings.point: а/б (criteria of one run that do not fit together, AP-016)
findings.where: REQ-108 criterion 11: app.yml `paths` «exactly app/**, tools/src/team/**, tools/src/pixel-office/mask.js and .github/workflows/app.yml»; REQ-109 criterion 9: app/test/unit/runbooks.test.js reads docs/runbooks/release.md and docs/runbooks/incident.md.
findings.problem: A test of the app check reads files outside the path filter that criterion 11 fixes as «exactly». A commit that changes only docs/runbooks/** (for example the flag fix expected after spike S1) does not start app.yml, and PLAN §4.3 asks for `cd app && npm run check` only «for app/ changes», so runbooks.test.js can turn red unseen by both. The same holds for any other input outside app/ that an app test reads (criterion 1 compares with the versions of tools/package.json if the test reads that file). The designer cannot add the path without breaking criterion 11.
findings.needed: Criterion 11's path list includes docs/runbooks/** and every other path an app test reads (or the block forbids app tests from reading outside app/ and moves the runbook check elsewhere).

findings.point: а (a vendor fact frozen in a criterion without a check, AP-076, AP-079)
findings.where: REQ-109 criterion 9: release.md holds «the rollback `npx vercel@<pin> rollback <previous production URL> --yes`».
findings.problem: Vercel's CLI reference for `vercel rollback` (https://vercel.com/docs/cli/rollback, read 2026-11-17, last_updated 2026-03-17; not measured) lists one unique option, `--timeout`, and global options without `--yes`. The criterion and its test pin a flag the vendor does not document into the runbook the owner uses during an incident; ARCH §19.5 itself says the exact flags are fixed by spike S1 in release.md, and after S1 the text cannot be corrected without changing this criterion (AP-079). The same page says that on Hobby only the previous production deployment can be rolled back, and that a rollback is undone with `vercel promote`, which «re-enables auto-assignment of production domains» — the next production deploy after a rollback is not described.
findings.needed: Criterion 9 pins only documented command forms (rollback without `--yes`), or pins the command names and the one exact pin and leaves the flags to S1 by reference; the release path names what follows a rollback (promote) or says it is fixed by S1.

findings.where: the secret grep of criterion 13 (a Postgres address with a password).

findings.where: the Node of the app.yml jobs; criterion 4 «With NODE_ENV=production and no DATABASE_URL … exit ≠ 0, one plain line».
findings.problem: The block does not name the Node version of app.yml. The smoke-local test of REQ-109 criterion 5 fails when /api/health reports node below v22.23.4, so a runner Node below the floor turns app.yml red; the current runner image caches 22.23.4 (actions/runner-images Ubuntu2404-Readme, image 20261111.370.1, read 2026-11-17, not measured), and decisions/0101 (Addition 2026-11-17) records that the runner cache gave v22.23.3 up to 2026-10-27. On such a Node the refusal of criterion 4 also passes for the floor line, not for the DATABASE_URL rule, since the line is not named.
findings.needed: Bind the app.yml Node to ≥ v22.23.4 and name the refusal line of criterion 4 (it names DATABASE_URL).

findings.where: migrate.test.js runs `node server/db/migrate.js` on PGlite, reads the tables, runs it again, and runs it on a temporary migrations folder.
findings.problem: An in-memory PGlite does not outlive the process; how the test points the process at a persistent PGlite folder and at another migrations folder (variables that criterion 13 then requires in .env.example) is not named. The Q9 lint binds `query(` only; PGlite's multi-statement `exec(` is a second SQL entry it does not see. Roles are cluster-wide in Postgres, so a 0001 that runs on a second database of the same server (the pg job, a Neon branch) must tolerate existing roles.
findings.needed: Design names the variables, the `exec(` rule and role creation that tolerates an existing role.

findings.problem: Criterion 15 keeps the server alive when the database is down at start, criterion 8 makes it exit on an unsafe role at start; when the selfcheck runs after the database comes back, and what the Vercel function (which cannot exit) does with an unsafe role besides health "unsafe", is not said. On PGlite the selfcheck reading is left to the design (decisions/0116 О10) — a measured point, but the pass value «role ok» of REQ-109 criterion 3 then rests on a reading the design names.
findings.needed: The design names both; the PGlite reading must not be reused on Postgres (covered if F1 adds the real-Postgres case).
